source_text: 5 DE FULMINE IPSIUS IOVIS AUDITE. Dicitis o stulti: Iouis tonat, fulminat ipse. Etsi paruulitas sic sensit, cur anni dicentes? Fuistis infantes: numquid et semper eritis? Uersari inmaturum infantia non capit <usus> Lusus puerilis cessit: sic et corda recedant; Moribus utique consilia uestra debentur. Insipiens ergo Iouem tonitruare tu credis Natum hic in terris et lacte caprino nutritum; Ergo si illum deuorasset <pater> Saturnus, In istis temporibus quis pluebat illo defuncto? Praesertim mortali patre deus nasci credatur? Saturnus in terris senuit et defecit in ipsis. Illum non aliquis prophetauit ante pronasci. Uel, si tonat ipse, lex ab ipso lata fuisset. Seducunt historiae, factus cum fue<rat ipse>. Ille autem in Cretam regnauit et ibi defecit. Omnipotens uobis factus Semelis amator. Uix ipse modo similiter amaret, si uiuere<t> ille. Inpuros oratis et dicitis esse caelestes Semine mortali natos de Gigantibus illis. Auditis et legitis natum in terra fuisse: Unde bene meruit corruptor ascendere caelum? Dicitis et fulmen Ciclopas illi fecissent. Inmortalis enim habuit a mortalibus arma. Tot reum criminibus, parricidam quoque suorum, Ex auctoritate uestra contulistis in altum.
pass_a_gloss: Iuppiter tonat? Leave infantia. Saturnus in terris senuit. Nemo prophetauit. Historiae seducunt. Impuros oratis… de Gigantibus. Parricidam… in altum.
pass_b_english: You say, O fools: Jupiter himself thunders and hurls lightning. Even if littleness felt so, why do years still say it? You were infants: will you be so forever? Infancy’s use does not take up mature turning; childish play has yielded — so let hearts also withdraw; your counsels are owed to character. Senseless, then, do you believe Jupiter thunders — born here on earth and nursed on goat’s milk? So if father Saturn had eaten him, in those times who was raining when he was dead? Especially — is a god believed born of a mortal father? Saturn grew old on earth and failed on it. No one prophesied him before he was born. Or, if he himself thunders, law would have been given by him. Histories seduce, when he himself had been made. But he reigned in Crete and failed there. The Omnipotent has been made for you Semele’s lover. Scarcely would he himself likewise love now, if that one lived. You pray to the impure and say they are celestial, born of mortal seed from those Giants. You hear and read he was born on earth: whence did a corrupter well deserve to climb heaven? You also say the Cyclopes made him a thunderbolt. For the immortal had arms from mortals. So guilty of crimes, a parricide of his own too — by your authority you have conferred him on high.

choices.why: Inpuros oratis et dicitis esse caelestes

choices.choose: do not lift a parricide on high
